tokens.headline: The Case for *Pink*
tokens.standfirst: Why the colour everyone is told to outgrow is the one I keep coming back to.

tokens.headline: Everyone thinks pink is the *easy* choice.
tokens.body: It’s the first colour we’re handed and the first we’re told to grow out of. Somewhere between a child’s bedroom and grown-up good taste, pink gets quietly retired.

tokens.headline: Then you see it done *properly*.
tokens.body: Not bubblegum, not blush by default. A pink with depth — coral leaning to rust, the soft chalk of a garden rose, a stem so deep it reads almost brown. Pink with the volume turned down.

tokens.headline: Soft, but not *sweet*.
tokens.standfirst: One palette, many tones — the range a single colour can hold when you let it.

tokens.quote:
Pink isn’t a mood.
It’s a whole *register*.

tokens.headline: Build it from the *deepest* tone first.
tokens.body: Start dark and work back toward the light, the way you’d layer a painting. The pale tones read as highlights then — earned, not assumed.

tokens.headline: One pink, repeated, reads *flat*.
tokens.body: It’s tone on tone that gives pink its richness. Three or four shades of the one colour will always feel considered beside a single, even pink.

tokens.headline: Pink, taken *seriously*.
tokens.body: It was never the colour that needed growing out of. It was the way we were using it.
